answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The ivory multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and haven lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1376 identities would post 4185 proofs and burn roughly 33 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
